extracted.intended_audience: Writers and production company staff preparing/submitting theatrical writing credits (WGA signatory)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedures and standards for preparing and submitting Notices of Tentative Writing Credits (NTWCs), assembling materials for credit arbitrations, and complying with WGA/MBA/SCM requirements for on-screen credits, cover pages, waivers, titles, and publicity for theatrical motion pictures.

rubrics_metrics.name: NTWC is essential and must be properly completed
rubrics_metrics.description: The NTWC is one of the most important documents a writer will receive; it serves multiple functions for the Guild, the writer, and the Company and must be properly completed and sent to participating writers and the Guild.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: sets mechanism for determination of credits so credits can be finalized; advises writers of proposed credit and deadline to protest or elect a pseudonym; offers the Guild an opportunity to ensure proposed writing and source material credits comply with the MBA and Guild policy; not a replacement for the MBA or the SCM. A sample NTWC is attached to the Guide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for NTWC submission
rubrics_metrics.description: The NTWC must be submitted to the Guild and to all participating writers as soon as practicable following completion of principal photography.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (TSA, ¶11.) Ensure timely filing so credits can be finalized; check other NTWC requirements before sending.

rubrics_metrics.name: List all participating writers (names and addresses)
rubrics_metrics.description: List the names and addresses of all participating writers at the top of the NTWC; you must list all participating writers even if they are not proposed for credit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (TSA, ¶9; SCM, pp. 4-5.) Definition: a participating writer is a writer who participated in the screenplay or was employed by the Company on story/screenplay or a professional writer who sold or licensed literary material subject to the MBA (see Article 1.B.1.b. of the MBA).

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmit NTWC by independently verifiable means (not email)
rubrics_metrics.description: The NTWC must be sent via Certified Mail/Return Receipt Requested, messenger, or some other independently verifiable means; e-mail is not considered independently verifiable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (TSA, ¶¶2, 12 and 17.) The NTWC must be sent to the writer unless a contract directs the Company to send it to an agent or other designated representative(s). Keep proof of delivery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include title and all production executives; indicate writer-as-executive status
rubrics_metrics.description: List the title of the motion picture and the names of all production executives, including director and all producers; indicate on the NTWC if a participating writer will also be credited as a production executive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give notice to all parties if a participating writer is also going to be credited as a production executive before writing credits are determined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed on-screen writing credit must include form of credit
rubrics_metrics.description: List the proposed on-screen writing credit and include the form of credit (e.g., “Written by”, “Screenplay by”), not just the writer name(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (TSA, ¶¶1–2; SCM, pp. 16–18.) Writers may only be credited in the manner set forth in the MBA unless a waiver is granted; consult the SCM or Credits Department for questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable writing credit forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Only certain forms of writing credit are allowable under the MBA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowable credits include “Written by,” “Screenplay by,” “Story by,” “Screen Story by,” “Adaptation by,” “Narration Written by” and “Based on Characters Created by.” Review the SCM or contact rrubin@wgaeast.org with questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combining writing credit with director/producer may require waiver
rubrics_metrics.description: In certain circumstances, the writing credit can be combined with the credit to the Director and/or the Producer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact the Credits Department to determine whether a waiver is required. (TSA, ¶¶3, 8.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Use ampersand for team authorship vs 'and' for separate writers
rubrics_metrics.description: Ampersand (&) is used between the names of writers who worked as a team; the word 'and' is used between names of writers who did not work as a team.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (SCM, pg. 2.) Teams are treated differently for crediting and arbitration rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include on-screen source material credit on NTWC
rubrics_metrics.description: Include any on-screen source material credit (e.g., “Based on the Novel by”) on the NTWC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (TSA, ¶2; SCM, pp. 16–17.) Note: generally the word 'Novel' denotes fiction and 'Book' denotes non-fiction. Include source material even if it will not appear on-screen.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include presentation/production credit to be accorded on screen/advertising
rubrics_metrics.description: Include on the NTWC any presentation and/or production credit to be accorded on screen and/or in advertising (e.g., “Universal Pictures Presents” or “A Film by”).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (TSA, ¶28.) This ensures the Guild can review such credits for MBA compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: List any and all source material (including prior films)
rubrics_metrics.description: List any source material submitted to or acquired by the Company, including prior motion pictures in the case of a remake or sequel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This helps the Guild determine appropriate source credits and whether the material is subject to the MBA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Send final shooting script to all participating writers
rubrics_metrics.description: Send a copy of the final shooting script to all participating writers, including those not proposed for credit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (TSA, ¶11.) Ensures transparency about the final shooting material used to determine credits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Properly calculate the finalization date for proposed credits
rubrics_metrics.description: Properly calculate the date on which proposed credits become final absent a protest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (TSA, ¶13.) Generally credits become final twelve business days from the date the NTWC is sent; may be shortened to seven business days if a good faith emergency exists and is requested on the NTWC. If automatic arbitration provisions apply, write 'Automatic Arbitration' in place of a final date.

rubrics_metrics.name: NTWC must include production company contact info and authorized signature
rubrics_metrics.description: List the name, address, telephone number of the production company and authorized representative and ensure the NTWC is signed by the authorized representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure authorized signatory signs the NTWC to validate it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Date sent must be the actual send date
rubrics_metrics.description: List the date on which the NTWC is sent to the Guild and participating writers; this must be the actual send date, not the preparation date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The send date triggers protest deadlines and arbitration timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaboration agreements required when production executive co-authors with non-production writer
rubrics_metrics.description: A Collaboration Agreement is required when a production executive writes in collaboration as a team with a non-production executive writer and the production executive intends to claim co-authorship of the team's material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (SCM, pg. 2.) A writing services agreement employing both writers as a team can serve as a Collaboration Agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team waivers required for writing teams of four or more
rubrics_metrics.description: A team waiver is required for writing teams of four or more people; a 'team' is generally no more than two writers (or three in certain Article 13.A.9 situations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (TSA, ¶4; SCM, pg. 2.) Waivers must be requested and approved in advance of services being performed; contact Contracts Department at rrubin@wgaeast.org to request a team waiver.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic arbitration triggers under the MBA
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain circumstances trigger automatic credit arbitration under the MBA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Automatic arbitration is triggered when: a production executive is proposed for writing credit with other non-production executive participating writers (TSA, ¶6; SCM, pg. 23); a 'Screen Story by' credit is proposed (TSA, ¶2.c.; SCM, pg. 19); an 'Adaptation by' credit is proposed (TSA, ¶1; SCM, pg. 22); or three writers are proposed for 'Written by' or 'Screenplay by' credit (TSA, ¶4; SCM, pp. 19–20). Note: a team is considered a single writer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arbitration submission materials and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: In arbitration, submit specified materials to the Guild as soon as possible (upon receipt of a protest or concurrently with NTWC in automatic arbitration).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (TSA, ¶18.) Required: three copies of all literary material submitted to or acquired by the Company by all participating writers and any source material. Literary material includes beatsheets, outlines, stories, treatments, scripts, formats, etc. Also submit a transmittal letter identifying each piece by author and date (sample attached). See SCM pages 4–15 for credit determination process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover pages on literary material must comply with MBA Article 37
rubrics_metrics.description: Cover pages on all literary material must comply with Article 37 of the MBA concerning names on literary material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Article 37.) Upon commencement of pre-production, the Company shall place the name of the initial writer on literary material, following which the word 'revisions' shall precede the names of all subsequent writers. A sample cover page is attached.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waivers required in specified circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: Guild waivers are required for certain activities and credit combinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: team waivers for teams of four+, screenings in advance of the Guild’s final determination of writing credits for film festivals or other public exhibitions require a waiver, and waivers are required to combine credits such as 'Written, Produced, and Directed by'; 'Written and Produced by'; and 'Written for the Screen and Directed by.' Contact rrubin@wgaeast.org to request waivers.

rubrics_metrics.name: On-screen placement rules for writing credits
rubrics_metrics.description: General rules govern where and how writing credits appear on screen relative to the director and among themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (TSA, ¶8.) Writing credit must appear on a separate card contiguous to the director's credit. Main title format: if 'Screenplay by' and 'Story by' appear on the same card, 'Screenplay by' must appear in the top 50% of the card; if on separate cards, 'Story by' must precede 'Screenplay by'. End title format: 'Screenplay by' always precedes 'Story by'. The writing credit must appear in the main titles if any personal names, or portions thereof (including initials), appear in the main titles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement rules for source material credit
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for placement of source material credit relative to writing and director credits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generally the source material credit may appear in main or end titles and should be on a separate card from the writing credit. If the source material author is also the sole credited writer of the screenplay, the source credit may appear on the same card as the writing credit. The source material credit may not be placed between the 'Screenplay by' credit and the director's credit when credits are on separate cards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit main and end titles to WGA for approval before prints
rubrics_metrics.description: You are required to submit the main and end titles for the picture to the WGA for approval before any prints are prepared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (TSA, ¶8.) Ensures on-screen credits conform to MBA provisions and avoids penalties for non-compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit all publicity and advertising material to WGA for approval prior to issuance
rubrics_metrics.description: All publicity and advertising material must be submitted to the WGA for approval prior to issuance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (TSA, ¶26.) Ensures publicity and advertising conform to MBA provisions and helps avoid penalties for non-compliance.
